text: Ben Siverly Product Manager · Proptech, Data Platforms & AI Technical PM · Recovering Data Scientist · Decisions in writing San Mateo, CA San Francisco Bay Area benjaminsiverly@gmail.com linkedin.com/in/be-ns github.com/be-ns · bensiverly.com Data scientist turned PM. Nearly four years in proptech. I turn messy, regulated data into decisions people can trust, for parties who don’t fully trust each other and can’t afford to be wrong. Experience AppFolio · Product Manager, Rental ApplicationsProduct Manager, Rental Applications & Payments Jan 2023 – Oct 2026 Property-management software for 23,000+ customers. Property-management software for 23,000+ customers. Sole PM for the rental application line, across two codebases. Property-management software. The rental application is where both sides meet: 9M+ applicants a year, 23,000+ property management companies, and $200M+ in application fees between them. Sole PM for the rental application: 9M+ application starts and $200M in fees processed a year, across two codebases. Led the rebuild: submission rose from 44% to 70%, and vacancies filled 3.4 days faster than offline workflows. Turned fair-housing and screening-compliance rules into product requirements. Kept applicant follow-up inside the authenticated app so every interaction is auditable; customer satisfaction rose 18%. Gated AI review of applicant ID uploads on an eval set of real and synthetic IDs. Releases shipped only when the model cleared quality bars on representative data. Shaped features as tools a workflow builder or a customer’s own agent can call, on data where AppFolio is the system of record. Launched a secure applicant-data API with Zillow (70% customer adoption), then pushed to wind it down when it flooded property managers with unqualified applicants. Adoption was not value. Sized offline rent from accounting-receipt data and renter interviews. Leadership funded two teams from the analysis: rent-split payments and a digital certified-funds partnership. Owned checkout for $200M a year in application fees, built on AppFolio’s internal payments API. 70% of applications carry an embedded payment: the applicant pays, the property manager acts on it. Designed an assumed-success window and a tokenized failed-payment recovery path, reaching 99.1% application-payment completion. On the payments team, sized offline rent from accounting receipts and interviewed renters on why they pay offline: irregular gig pay, unbanked renters driving 15–30 minutes for certified funds, 2–3 day ACH. Presented to payments leadership, who funded teams to build rent-split payments with Flex and a digital certified-funds partnership. Rebuilt the rental application end to end. Submission rates went from 44% to 70%, and properties on the new flow fill vacancies 3.4 days faster than offline workflows. Kept follow-up inside the authenticated app so every interaction stays auditable for screening compliance; customer satisfaction rose 18%. Built a secure applicant-data API and launched it with Zillow. Reached 70% customer adoption, then pushed to wind it down when the frictionless path buried property managers in unqualified applicants. Sole PM for the application line: strategy and roadmap for applicants and property managers across two codebases that ship together. The payer and the user are different people, and the product has to serve both. Every customer runs its own configuration, so each change had to hold across thousands of setups. Rebuilt the rental application end to end. Submission rate went from 44% to 70% with a zero change-failure rate, and units on the new flow fill 3.4 days faster than offline workflows. Redesigned the payment step, built on AppFolio’s internal payments API, around how callbacks actually arrive. Modeled the latency tail, moved the wait from 8 to 12 seconds, and sent the long tail to an authenticated recovery link instead of a longer spinner. Timeouts fell from ~8% to ~4%; payment completion reached about 99%. Built an API that moves applicant PII between platforms to pre-fill applications. Launched with Zillow and reached 70% customer adoption, then pushed to wind it down: volume went up, and property managers got buried in unqualified applicants. More applicants did not mean better matches. Built a verified jobs-to-be-done map from 50–100 customer calls a year: one shared model of what renters and property managers need, later the corpus for an internal RAG tool. Every product bet traces back to it. Shipped follow-up for incomplete applications inside the authenticated app, not over email or text, so every interaction stays auditable for fair-housing compliance. Customer satisfaction on rental applications rose 18%. Moved my team to spec-driven work: behavior written and pressure-tested before code, every release gated on tests and evals. Lively · Data Scientist → Product Manager Nov 2019 – Dec 2022 HSA platform offered through financial-institution partners. 45-person Series B. HSA platform for tax-advantaged health spending, offered through financial-institution partners. HSA platform. Partners on one side, account holders on the other, money moving between banks underneath. First data hire. Stood up the data platform end to end: ingestion, data modeling, BI, product analytics. Promoted to PM in 2021 when the platform became the roadmap. Shipped partner APIs and migration pipelines that moved $50M+ in assets between financial institutions with zero data loss. Cut the work from two migration teams to one. Designed the partner data model and ledgers behind bank and card-network transfers. Scoped multi-tenancy with our second partner bank’s executives, capturing ~90 bps more yield on AUM as rates rose. Built the money-movement platform: bank and card-network transfers, processor integrations, ledgers, and the partner data model. Financial-institution partners could offer compliant HSAs without building their own infrastructure. Scoped multi-tenancy with our second partner bank’s executives. The move captured ~90 bps more yield on AUM as rates rose, and opened room for future partners. Built partner APIs and migration pipelines that moved $50M+ in HSA assets between financial institutions with zero data loss. Cut the work from two migration teams to one. Stood up the company’s first data-science function and data-services platform; promoted to PM in 2021 as the work became the roadmap. Built the partner APIs and migration pipelines that moved $50M+ in HSA assets across financial institutions with zero data loss, cutting the work from two migration teams to one. Built the platform under it: money movement across banks and card networks, processor integrations, ledgers, and the data model partners built on, so they could offer compliant HSA accounts without building the infrastructure themselves. Stood up the first data-science function and data platform; promoted to PM in 2021 as the work became the roadmap. Oracle · Data Scientist, Applied Research Sep 2017 – Sep 2019 Found and corrected a sampling skew that distorted model performance; rebuilt validation on a representative U.S. population sample. Automated a pipeline that took two analysts full-time. Rebuilt model validation on a representative U.S. population sample, correcting a skew that distorted model performance. Automated a data pipeline that had taken two analysts full-time. Rebuilt the model-validation methodology on a representative U.S. population sample, correcting a data skew that had distorted how we measured model performance. Automated the ad-viewability pipeline (Python, JIRA API), replacing extraction and cleaning that took two analysts full-time. Earlier. Second hire at Olivers Apparel, a DTC menswear startup: textile R&D and fabric cost modeling. Selected AI Product WorkSelected Work Housing as an API call (in progress). Side project: given capital and a target market, map parcels, use LLMs to extract buildable envelopes from city zoning codes, and estimate whether a project pencils. Brava (bravamade.com). Recruiting profiles for youth athletes, built with my brother. AI pipeline: coach-verified stats in, benchmark rankings and generated media out. Ran a COPPA privacy review; built with AI coding agents. AbiertoClaw (github.com/be-ns/AbiertoClaw). Open-source Hermes Agent plugin that picks the best free model daily and falls back to a local model. Brava (bravamade.com). Automated college-recruiting profiles for youth athletes, launching with women’s soccer outside major metros. Built with my brother. Sized the market across five sports, ran a COPPA and privacy review for minors’ data, and built the AI production pipeline: coach-verified stats, benchmark rankings, generated media. Payments on Stripe: a parent checkout flow built from scratch with AI coding agents. AbiertoClaw (github.com/be-ns/AbiertoClaw). Open-source plugin for the Hermes agent. Each day it finds the best free model that passes a real tool-call test and switches Hermes to it, with a local model as the fallback. Brava (bravamade.com). Recruiting profiles that help women’s soccer athletes outside the major metros get seen by college coaches. Built with my brother and live with customers. Coach-verified stats, benchmark rankings, an AI-assisted production pipeline. Designed and shipped it myself, from the first research call to the brand on the page. AbiertoClaw (github.com/be-ns/AbiertoClaw). Open-source AI agent that runs our family calendar over iMessage. A complexity router and a daily best-free-model picker keep it free by default.
